Question_text: A car approaches a set of traffic lights. The lights change to red at time t = 0. Fig. 2.1 shows how the speed of the car changes with time.
image: Fig. 2.1 is a speed-time graph. The x-axis is time (t/s) from 0 to 8s. The y-axis is speed (m/s) from 0 to 24 m/s. The graph shows a horizontal line at 20 m/s from t=0 to t=2s, indicating constant speed. From t=2s to t=7s, the speed decreases from 20 m/s to 0 m/s along a curve, which becomes steeper towards the end, indicating non-uniform deceleration. After t=7s, the speed remains 0 m/s.

Parts.part_text: The car starts to slow down a short time after the lights change to red. Determine the time between the lights changing to red and the car starting to slow down.
State what is meant by uniform acceleration.
State how Fig. 2.1 shows that the deceleration of the car between t = 2s and t = 7s is non-uniform.
Determine the distance the car travels from the moment the car starts to slow down until it stops.

Question_text: Fig. 5.1 shows a method of producing sandpaper using static electricity. Glue is sprayed on to moving paper. The sticky paper then passes between two metal plates. One of the plates is positive and the other plate is negative. There is an electric field between the plates. Grains of sand are present just below the sticky paper. Each grain of sand is a conductor of electricity. Fig. 5.3 shows two layers of sand grains in the space between the two plates. A student receives an electric shock by walking across a certain type of carpet and then nearly touching a piece of earthed metal with his hand. The potential difference between the hand and the metal is 2000V and the charge transferred is 4.0 × 10⁻⁴ C.
image: Fig. 5.1 illustrates a process for producing sandpaper using static electricity, showing glue on paper passing between negative and positive metal plates, with sand attracted upwards to the paper. Parts.part_text: On Fig. 5.2, draw the electric field between the two metal plates. Show the direction of the electric field.
Parts.image: Fig. 5.2 shows two parallel, angled metal plates. The upper plate is labeled 'negative metal plate' and the lower plate is labeled 'positive metal plate'. This is an empty diagram for drawing electric field lines.

State why the top layer of sand moves towards the sticky paper.
Calculate the energy transferred when the spark jumps across the air gap from the metal onto his hand.
